title: draft - b7f92e4d
description:
Amazon purchase histories contain broad taste signals that can survive even when purchase order is noisy. The existing attempts explore graph propagation and sequential ranking; this proposal tests a different hypothesis: reconstructing a user’s purchases from a corrupted, unordered history can learn useful item affinities. Each category receives its own multinomial variational autoencoder, replacing the SASRec architecture while preserving dataset routing and the supplied splits. Sparse history encoding avoids allocating dense input matrices, while the decoder learns competition across the complete item catalog.

Training uses only training interactions, with input dropout and an annealed variational penalty to discourage memorization. Inference uses the deterministic posterior mean and scores candidates through the trained decoder. Checkpoints are selected using validation HR@10 on 200 users with 99 unique negatives and seed 42, with NDCG@10 breaking ties. A macro-average above the supplied 0.505 baseline would support the unordered-preference hypothesis; weaker results would suggest that order or explicit collaborative propagation matters more. The script writes the matching working/predict.py for host evaluation; hidden test access and submission generation remain with the host.
method: Trains a separate multinomial VAE for each of four dataset routes. Binary, deduplicated histories enter a sparse, length-normalized EmbeddingBag encoder with 50% input dropout, a 256-unit hidden layer, and a 64-dimensional Gaussian latent representation. A nonlinear decoder reconstructs purchases across the full catalog using multinomial loss plus an annealed KL penalty capped at 0.2. Adam trains the models; local validation HR@10 selects checkpoints, with NDCG@10 breaking ties and early stopping after 25 epochs without improvement. The generated predictor loads matching category checkpoints and scores candidates using the deterministic posterior mean. Training reads only supplied training and validation splits, retains GAGC_DATA_DIR, and saves artifacts under the trial's working directory.
